{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Northwind / Brightline)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (for Customer)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement  
**Findings reviewed:** 18 rules — 16 compliant, 2 deviations, 0 missing

---

## Executive summary

This draft is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us. The high-value protections all sit at or above our preferred position: Vendor's IP and data indemnity is uncapped by virtue of the Excluded Claims carve-out (§ 20, § 21.3); we own Deliverables and retain all Customer Data with a perpetual, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor Technology (§§ 13–15); we hold an unconditional 30-day termination-for-convenience right with a prepaid-fee refund and no early-termination fee (§ 9.4, § 29.4, § 10.2); assignment, licence scope, warranties, insurance, audit, renewal and transition assistance all meet the playbook. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, non-solicit or Customer-side MFN obligation anywhere in the document, and § 12.3 affirmatively confirms as much. Governing law and venue are New York, as preferred, with no arbitration clause.

Two deviations remain, and both trace back to the same drafting defect. "Fees" is defined at §§ 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, even though the term is used throughout to mean recurring and Order Form fees (§§ 7.1, 8.3, 10.2). The consequence is that the mutual liability cap in § 21.1 — already narrowed to amounts under "the first Order Form" — collapses to roughly USD 12,000 regardless of actual spend, which fails even our fallback. Separately, § 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on us of 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment, uncapped and triggered by a minor breach; that is walk-away territory under the playbook. We should treat the defective "Fees" definition as a document-wide fix, since read literally it would also narrow our § 9.4 refund right.

**Verification note:** the proposed redline to § 21.1 did not pass automated verification and requires manual drafting before it goes back to Vendor. The § 7.7 redline was repaired and verified.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |
| Low | **LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer** | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| Low | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs** | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability (§ 21.1) |

### Deviation detail

**§ 7.7 — Liquidated damages payable by Customer (LD).** Liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay, triggered by late payment of any invoice and uncapped, can quickly exceed remaining contract value. Our preferred position is no Customer-payable liquidated damages; the fallback is a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees. Because § 9.4 carries no early-termination fee, no capped LD amount is needed elsewhere. *Proposal:* convert § 7.7 so that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer for late payment, replaced by ordinary late-payment interest on undisputed amounts. Service credits running in our favour are unaffected. Verified (repaired).

**§ 21.1 — Cap basis (LOL-CAP).** Mutuality and the § 21.3 Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) plus the payment-obligation carve-back all meet the preferred position. The cap *basis* does not: with "Fees" defined as the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee and the cap further limited to the first Order Form, the ceiling is illusory and falls below even a six-month fee fallback. *Proposal:* re-base the mutual cap on amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim, with a USD 1,000,000 floor, and confirm Customer's payment obligations are not damages — leaving mutuality, exclusions and Excluded Claims untouched. **Verification failed; redline to be drafted manually before issue.**

---

## Walk-away items

1. **§ 7.7 liquidated damages.** An uncapped 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week penalty triggered by a minor payment breach is walk-away territory under the playbook. Removal of the penalty mechanic (interest only on undisputed late amounts) is a condition of signature.
2. **§ 21.1 cap basis.** A liability ceiling of approximately USD 12,000 irrespective of actual spend is effectively illusory and fails our fallback. A 12-month paid-or-payable basis with a meaningful floor is required; we should not proceed on the current basis.

---

## Next steps

1. **Manually draft the § 21.1 redline** and re-verify before the markup goes out, given the failed verification on the automated proposal.
2. **Issue the § 7.7 redline** removing Customer-payable liquidated damages in favour of interest on undisputed late amounts.
3. **Raise the "Fees" definition as a document-wide fix.** Sections 1.5/1.6 define "Fees" as the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee only, which is inconsistent with §§ 7.1, 8.3, 10.2 and 21.1, and read literally would narrow our § 9.4 refund. Align the definition with recurring and Order Form fees; this is the cleanest single amendment and resolves the root cause of both deviations.
4. **Confirm no further redlines.** The remaining 16 rules are compliant and should not be reopened; the Vendor-granted MFN (§ 7.6), the Vendor-side competing-service restriction (§ 12.4) and the § 24.4 change-of-control protections run in our favour and should be preserved as drafted.
5. **Note for the business (no action in the markup):** the § 9.4 convenience-termination notice period sits in § 29.4 rather than in § 9.4 itself — substantively correct but worth flagging to the contract owner for operational clarity.
"}
